text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Smart Phone - Gray, pretend phone musical infant toy with lights and learning content Let me first say I love this toy and think it is a great concept BUT it does not work well. When we received it new, it did work however the volume is VERY low and there are no volume adjustment options. You basically have to hold the phone up to your ear to hear it (which obviously isn't great for little ones who don't quite understand that concept yet). Despite it being low, we just kept it and dealt with it rather than the hassle of returning. However today the volume/sound stopped working altogether (after ~1 month of use). The buttons still light up but no sound comes out. I tried changing the batteries however it continues to not work. Of course it is past the return window. My advice to buyers is to maybe try it out in the store first before ordering here. I am not sure if I just got a defective one or if the volume is just designed low on this toy. Really wish it worked as intended because my son would love it!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Smart Phone - Gray, pretend phone musical infant toy with lights and learning content

text_fidelity_a:
CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question Excellent party game from the makers of Codenames. If you've played Codenames, then you know that is a fantastic party game, but that it requires the right group - a slow or domineering player can often mean that everyone is standing around staring at the board for an hour while they dole out perfectly configured clues. It's a fun game, but it requires the right group. That's a Question is a party game that can be played by absolutely anyone, and that, in my opinion, makes it almost a superior game.

In That's a Question!, players use cards to ask A/B style "would you rather" questions in which players attempt to guess the outcome. Based on the results, you move your pawn along the track.

The rulebook is well-written and funny, and is aware that this game is a little bit weird - attempting to give a theme to a basic Q&A style game, but it works. Of course, the game is not perfect. You are limited to only asking three different main questions, although the game does provide a wide variation of answers. There are also point modification questions which allow you to muddy up the scoring in your favor. Ultimately, the scoring was the part of the game that we found most cumbersome, and the modifiers didn't help that, simply adding a little more chaos. Scoring is also modified based on how many players are playing; as this was clearly designed as a 5-6 player game, a 4-player game has a few modifications, and the 3-player game has a fairly substantial number of scoring modifications to make it more challenging. It's nothing you can't figure out, but it is not very clean.

Overall, a good party game for 5-6. The box indicates that this is a game for ages 15+, and nothing in the content of the cards makes me think that anyone from age 7 and up can't handle.
text_fidelity_b: CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question

Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ At the time of this review, this set is under $10. If it were over $10, I would probably subtract a star. This is definitely beginner, student quality.
But if you have a child, or maybe you are just looking for something reasonably priced to see if you enjoy sketching, even though it's geared for children, this set can't be beat.

The main reason it gets five stars, is that you get four different hardness levels of graphite pencils. Perfect for experimenting with your creativity and making a sketch come alive. And it's less messy than charcoal sticks, so once again, it's the perfect introduction to nurture a child's creativity and talent.
To make it even better, there's a little pamphlet to encourage and explain how to get your feet wet. I really like that the emphasis is on the fact that there are no mistakes, that each line is is just fine. So important for children that might be discouraged that they aren't instantly a great artist, forgetting or not understanding that being an artist is only 10% talent and 90% learning and desire.
It might be only a folded over page, but it covers various techniques. All is written in a way that kids and young adults can easily follow. This set is cured for ages 7 and up.
And once again, a 7-year-old doesn't need professional quality pencil sharpeners or paper. You can see in the photograph how thin the paper pages are, and how cheesy the little pencil sharpener is. Cheesy, but perfect for the purpose.

This well thought out set is just what I would expect from Farber-Castell. Their supplies are favored by the students and professionals worldwide.

I hope that this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not this set is right for you or a special child. Kids seem to be passionate about something one minute, and totally change the next. This little set is a very small investment, but of course, little investments add up.

xxoo

Tenergy TB6-B Balance Charger Discharger 1S-6S Digital Battery Pack Charger for NiMH/NiCD/Li-PO/Li-Fe Packs LCD Hobby Battery Charger w/ Tamiya/JST/EC3/HiTec/Deans Connectors + Power Supply 01435 This unit comes with almost everything you need to --

-- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. [[ASIN:B00JBP32A0 JST JST-XH 3S Balance Wire Extention 20cm adapter 11.1v LiPo Battery Cable Li-Po]] This also allows you to put the cells into a fireproof bag during charging. [[ASIN:B005Q3VSZC Bluecell Black Medium Size Lipo Battery Guard Sleeve/Bag for Charge & Storage]]

One other accessory that really helps is a compact voltage indicator [[ASIN:B003Y6E6IE Integy C23212 Lipo Voltage Checker/Warning Buzzer]] that you plug into the balance port on the battery. Not strictly needed for recharging, but is very useful to monitor voltage after charging.

You'll need to consult YouTube for useful instructions on how to manipulate the four buttons and why, unless you want to read the manual. And who reads manuals anymore when a good ten minute video is clearer and simpler?

Astronaut and Space Toy Action Figure Playset- 60 Piece set includes Astronauts, Rockets, Spaceship Shuttle, Rovers, Satellites and More - Great for imaginative play, school projects and dioramas Description states 50 astronauts. I have 43. And it totals 60 pieces with all the other parts. The lunar rovers are awesome and there are two seated figures to drive them.

This is a total mashup of different time periods of space exploration. Apollo-ish type rockets minus the needles. 2 great fairly accurate moon landing rovers, some type of sky lab, 2 nice space shuttles, 1 cool lunar lander and 2 American flags with stands. 2 flags makes no sense to me but ok. I wish there were boosters for the shuttles but that isnt a deal breaker.

So to people complaining there are no female astronauts in this set, tell your kids they are in the shuttles because that is the time period for U.S. women in space in this bucket of mashed up time periods. The moon walking men might be in Gemini style suits....no women wore those or walked around on the moon then. There isnt anything really historically accurate here as a whole but it really is a fun collection of space stuff.

There are 10 different poses for the figures I got with mulitples of each. All the figures look great, no flashing or deformities. I am sure they are copies of old figures. Giger counter guy, camera guy, radio, briefcase and more.

This is a very nice set. The price is a little too much but I havent seen this on shelves anywhere. I recommend it for kids and old "kids".

text_fidelity_a:
4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens My kids like their science, particularly my youngest who envisions, among other things, working for the government and taking part in the first mission to Mars. So, given my kids interest in all things scientific, the Tin Can Edge Detector looked like something they would enjoy building and examining from a scientific point of view.

Putting this little machine together takes some effort and one reason it takes more work than it should is the instructions. They are not written as clearly as they should be. It would not have been that difficult for the manufacturer to get this right, but it seems they put little effort into it. You have to supply your own battery and a can, but most importantly, you have to be patient and give it time. It’s also best to have an adult take charge, as young children will grow frustrated if they attempt this on their own.

Once assembled, you just place the robot on a table and let it do its thing. As expected, it moves across the surface until it detects an edge, then it reverses itself. It seemed to have no trouble doing what it claimed, and that is detecting when it reached the table’s edge and not falling off. In that respect, the robot functions as it should.

Now, what about the science? Well, It can teach a little bit about robotics, but that is about the extent of the educational value. There isn’t much else to it. Oh, and green advocates will like that it requires you to provide your own soda can because it encourages recycling

Science is a popular subject with my kids but they had a difficult time getting fired up over the Tin Can Edge Detector. The problem, from a kid’s perspective, is that it doesn’t really do enough to make it interesting. Simply crawling around on a table and not falling off just didn’t cut it for my kids. Adults will dislike the assembly more than anything and the limited educational value is also a drawback. Still, it does offer kids and parents an excuse to spend a little time together and it does what the manufacturer claims, so I’m going to give it a middle rating and a passing grade. There are better educational toys, but there is enough here to keep kids semi- interested for a low price.
text_fidelity_b: 4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens

SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories We had so much fun with this. While we did not do the whole party element with people watching us unbox, we had a great time just on a normal day when the kids had done a great job, having a special treat of opening up each of the flaps to see what was inside.

A glow-in-the-dark boo, another boo, both with movable arms, a skeleton for around the plant and a dry bones were the highlights for us in this set. The Princess peach, also was detailed to an extent I have never seen on any of our other Princess peach figures. Usually they just fill in and under her skirt with solid plastic, and this one they gave her legs, undershorts, and high-heeled shoes underneath her dress so it is much more of a realistic figure than usual. I think either Mario or Luigi, needed a little plastic stand to be able to stand up and not just topple over. I would've appreciated a little more design on those guys so that they could be played with without an additional little clear plastic stand.

The flap opening and unveiling of the characters was a lot of fun. The characters were almost impossible in some cases to get out of the container without completely destroying the entire packaging, so my kids had to be flexible to wait until we were done opening all the flaps, then tear open the packaging to be able to push from the back and get some of those characters out. However, they were definitely firmly and securely packaged in there and were not going anywhere or getting damaged with those vacuum formed spots to sit.

Overall this was a lot of fun, and with the excellent quality of the figures, made for a very special and memorable gifting event to the kids.
text_fidelity_b: SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Short version of the review: it’s a fun game with a pretty good first-game learning curve that settles in pretty quickly in subsequent games. It can be long (though you can adjust it). We’ll add it to our rotation of “lengthy” games

Longer version

1) Packing
I’m going to ding the game for packaging because while everything comes fine (as is typical, there’s a lot of popping pieces out of their cardboard sheets), I like when games include easy ways of keeping thing together and/or organized once you’ve played the first game. Even if it’s as minimal as separate small plastic bags. We used our own tiny bags (we’ve learned to keep ones that do come with other games if they’re extra thanks to consolidation) and a few regular small baggies, but I don’t think it’s too much to ask that those things be included

2) Materials
All the materials seem of good quality. Cards are not super-thick but they’re not at all flimsy, the non-plastic pieces feel solid and you don’t have any sense that they’ll start coming apart or getting dented/torn. The plastic cities are a nice touch, but the capital cities could perhaps have been made a little more distinctive. Not at all a big deal; a close look is all you need.

3) Instructions
The big sheet of instructions is fine. Generally clear and well written, with a few “clarification” points at the end, which is a nice touch. We had a few questions that weren’t included, but they were easy to find online. A few individual player cards with a stripped down bit of instruction for quick, easy reference would have been nice to toss in

4) Set up
As noted (and as is usual for these types of games) there’s a lot of popping things out and organizing. Once that’s done the first time, set-up is relatively quick. You put together some map tiles which is easy enough (though this 50+-year-old wouldn’t have minded if the organizing numbers were a little bigger on each tile). Each player gets tokens, a set of cards five of which are laid out in a particular order under their “Focus” bar (the cards are in these areas: Military, Technology, Culture, Economy, Industry), a set of “diplomacy” cards, a “leader” card (who they “play”—Cleopatra for instance), a few caravans (little wagons used for trading). After you’ve done it a few times it’s a pretty quick set-up. You also set up some cards to the side of the play area (World Wonder cards and City-State Diplomacy Cards and Victory Cards (these are what determine how the game is won). This is always an issue in these sorts of game because of course they’re not going to be truly “visible” to all the players. Someone is going to have to move or ask to see them to see what they say (some change throughout the game). I have no idea how to get around that though; it’s just a matter of physical setting.

5) game play
I’m not going to detail it. But generally, the Victory cards have two “agendas” on them, such as build two Wonders of the World, and a player who achieves one agenda from each of the cards is the winner (this is nice because you can shorten the game if desired by simply playing with fewer Victory cards). As far as the play itself
1) Players can “resolve” (do what it says) any one of the five cards below their Focus bar. This might mean building a city, attacking someone, moving a caravan, laying out a “Control” piece to claim a hex space (i.e. territory).
2) Once they’ve done that, that card gets move to slot one under the bar and all the others move one slot to the right. This is key because the slot number affects how the card is resolved. For instance, when you attack using your military card, you roll a die and add the slot number (and possibly other bonuses) to your roll. So you’re going to want to attack when that card is in the 4 or 5 position typically, not the 1 or 2 slot. This adds a nice bit of complexity to your action choices.

That’s pretty much the gameplay for players. A few other factor include
1) You can swap out a card under your focus by advancing your “Tech” counter a certain number (you do that using one of the cards). Once you hit a certain level, you can exchange one low level card for one that’s a bit more powerful. There are 4 levels of cards.
2) Barbarian tokens on the board move at regular periods and they can end up destroying one of your caravans or claiming territory from you (which affects how much money your cities earn and how much you can advance)
3) Caravans allow you to gain trade tokens that can be used to increase the impact of your cards. For example, if you have two trade tokens on your military card, you can spend one or both to add a bonus to your roll. Caravans can also garner you another player’s Diplomacy card, which has certain benefits dependent on the card.
4) Placing a control tokens mean you’ve claimed territory (that particular space), which is necessary for collecting trade tokens (a “mature” city garners you a set number of trade tokens once you’ve “controlled” all adjacent tiles), collecting resources such as marble or diamonds, or for building cities (your build cities a certain number of spaces from a space you’ve controlled with a token).
5) The terrain has an impact on your choices. In order of scaled “easiness”, the terrains are 1-grasslands, 2-hills, 3-forest, 4-desert, and 5-mountains. To travel through a desert is considered difficult, so that 4 means your Economy card (the one that moves your caravan) needs to be in the 4 or 5 slot. Similary, to build a city in a mountain space means your Industry card has to be in the 5 slot.

There are more rules and factors that come into play, but that’s the general gist. As noted at the start, I’d say the learning curve is relatively steep the first time ( a lot of going back to the instruction booklet), but past the first game or two, it comes pretty easily. I’ve certainly played games with a far steeper curve and one that takes longer to get to know game play well. If I were ranking learning curves on a ten-point scale, I’d probably put this around a 6.

Turns move slowly the first time or two as people try to remember what they can do, what they need to do, etc. But after the first hour each player moves pretty quickly through their turns as you’ve gotten used to how to deal with the complexities of those shifting slots under the Focus bar. As people get closer to each other, things slow again as players try and figure out cost-benefit of attacking, but then as before, after a few attacks those move quickly.

I liked the game quite a bit. More than my two family members, but I tend to have more patience for the slowness of things and I mind long game less than they do. They did like it enough to play again. And as mentioned, I like that you can self-adjust your length simply by cutting out one of the agendas. It’s a game we’ll definitely keep and keep playing.
text_fidelity_b: Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

It is also geared toward younger kids, but my younger kids have a tendency to pull the slides off and mess them up and then they don't have the ability to fix the problem. So, I hear, "MOM!!!!!" constantly while they are playing with this toy.

I am tired of hearing the "What time is it?" song. You think hearing the cartoon is bad, wait until they can bring the song to life on command. Oy!

The kids like the toy. It is very closed ended. They don't use their imaginations much. But the kids laugh and have some fun. If your kid just loves Bubble Guppies, and you love electronic toys- go right ahead.

Grandma- let me give you some advice. Your daughter-in-law will love you if you buy quiet plush Bubble Guppies instead. She'll love you even more if you spring for a nice set of blocks. Unless this toy was specifically asked for, avoid it!

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do activities, and then the parent will secretly leave another activity in the fairy house. This is suppose to make the child believe the fairies left them a gift. (For example: The child is to craft 3 fairy bells and hang them around their room. Inside the fairy house, they'll place a stick, pebbles, and a leaf. They'll then spin the house and ring each bell to summon a fairy visit.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids. In my opinion, there's more in the wizard kit. There is the same amount of activities in both, but there's just not as much to do in this fairy kit. (It seems more stickers and easy crafts.) It's not high quality, but it's still nice enough. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there'd the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though the wizard kit that is similar to this one could work for boys and girls(and this one still could, if desired), this fairy kit is definitely targeted to girls. At the end, I couldn't help but feel sorry for all the little children doing these activities, hoping to see a fairy. While gifts are left, which are supposed to let the child know a fairy visited them, they'll never actually see one, unless the parent does something extra. We just did the crafts, since we don't do imaginary things as real. Without the added magical element, though, this kit just doesn't hold near as much value. If you're like us and don't do Santa and all, I'd recommend another kind of kit. If you do love the idea of pretending fairies are leaving gifts, this might be a blast for you and your child, as long as you don't think they'll be too disappointed that they never actually see a fairy. Overall, I found it a little disappointing, particularly considering the current price(which changes constantly).
text_fidelity_b: Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Jurassic World Jurassic Park: T. rex Rampage 75936 Building Kit (3120 Pieces) At first glance, the Lego Jurassic World T. Rex Rampage is an impressive set. It’s geared towards older builders (16+), but I would say anyone could handle it.

The set has a lot of bags and 2 thick instruction books. The first book builds the T. Rex, the second book builds the Jurassic Park gate/scenes. There’s also a sticker sheet, which I was quite disappointed to see. In a set this pricey, Lego really should have printed a Jurassic Park tile. The sticker is the main focal point on the front of the gate, so if it’s not applied perfectly, it just doesn’t look great. Lego printed a similar size tile for an Ideas set, so I don’t think it’s too crazy to suggest they should have done it for Jurassic Park!

I also wish Lego had considered how the set would be displayed. Yes, you can play with this set, but I am sure most older builders like me are building it to show it off. I personally think the scene vignettes on the *back* of the gate are cooler than the front of the gate. At least they did think of the buildable stand for the minifigs, that’s a nice touch.

By the way, the minifigures are amazing. Great detail and major thumbs up on them.

The T. Rex was my favorite part of building the set. I knew how big he was going to be since measurements are included, but knowing versus seeing are two different things. Many of his joints are ball and socket, so he can be posed in a variety of ways. But at the same time, due to the weight of his various parts, he doesn’t always stay in those poses. For example, his head often falls forward. Small parts like his toe claws fall off easily, so watch if he’s played with. I had his head and tail come off multiple times when I was trying to pose him for display. He’s delicate.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Jurassic World Jurassic Park: T. rex Rampage 75936 Building Kit (3120 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a toy made with greenness in mind. It is manufactured with recycled materials and is great for environmentally- conscious parents who wants their kids to have some creative fun while also minimizing environmental impact. Designed for children between the ages of three and six, it is one of the few building toys that doesn't involve blocks or other interlocking rectangular pieces.

This toy involves building arrangements of flowers on a green, branch like base and there is no end to the different number of creative arrangements that kids can make. The pieces consist of leaves and three different flowers and they can be stacked and arranged in any number of ways. The combinations are endless and every time my girls play, it turns into a new adventure. My girls love creative toys, flowers, and art, so a toy like this is very likeable and enjoyable to them.

I like that this toy is made using recycled materials and I like the small, cube- shaped box included for storage. Most manufacturers do not even think about including a small storage box, and this often forces parents to use plastic bags or plastic containers to store the pieces. With an included box, there is no need to reach for these environmentally- unfriendly storage receptacles that may one day wind up in a landfill. Instead, you just use the included box, which is also made from recycled material, and the pieces will be safe to use for the next adventure.

With its lack of batteries, green composition, and creative encouragement, this toy is certainly a nice change from most others, but does it have any possible flaws or potential issues? I can think of only a few. One is the small pieces. They can easily become misplaced, so parents need to watch closely to make sure that kids place all of the pieces back into the box. Of course, the nice fact here is that you can afford to lose a few because, since they are all interchangeable, it won't prevent the toy from being used again and again. Another issue is that this toy could become boring after a while. There are those youngsters who crave action, lights, and sounds in their toys and if yours is one of them, then they may grow tired of the toy in a short time.

Recycling is certainly a good idea and creative toys that require imagination and not so much of the lights and sounds so common with kids' toys today are definitely a nice change of pace. Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a very nice little toy from Green Toys and it makes a great choice for these reasons. The possible building combinations are endless and while some kids may tire of it in a short time, it still has enough positive qualities and creative entertainment value to make it worth a purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games

text_fidelity_a:
Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.
text_fidelity_b: Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches

text_fidelity_a:
IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens What a great creative art toy. You can do literally anything with this and takes your sketches off the paper and into three dimensions. I am amazed at the ways the kids put this into practice, and it kept them engrossed for hours with only a couple squabbles over people hogging this color or that. I'll get more into what we did below. But first, What you get and How this works.

This product is a hardening gel that can be squeezed into shapes using plastic forms. There are several forms that come with the kit, a flat sheet of plastic and a couple rounded forms for creating spherical shapes. The flat clear piece is great for tracing images so even young kids can achieve the shapes they desire. Also, we used it to make other curves to help flesh out animal shapes, but that proved a little more difficult.

Once you have drawn your shapes with one of the gel pens, you can use the UV flashlight to harden the pieces to make them retain the shapes you want. Then you can peel them off the plastic forms or sheet and cement elements together into three dimensional structures. The possibilities are endless and only limited by creativity. Our kids started out by tracing the provided dinosaurs and moved on to tracing other dinos from various books until they had a small forest of dinos and trees.

Warnings and caveats: I'm a little leery of the chemically nature of this toy. There are warnings to avoid skin contact in light. This put me a little on edge and I wanted to supervise our 8 through 14 year olds to make sure it was not getting on skin or other stuff. Also, this does take a bit of artistic ability. It can be as free form as you want it to be, but we did have some frustration when younger kids could not recreate the stuff the older kids were building. But for the most part it was very conducive to creativity.

Also, the end products are a little sticky. So they don't seem like you can play with your creations, but you can make wonderful visual art. We have a nice little dino diorama on our book shelf now and the kids seem pretty proud of it. The inks are also a little messy, so make sure your in a cleanable area.

Personally, I think this is one of the most wonderfully novel and creative ideas I've seen in a while. I will be picking up some for the kids on my Christmas list, and look forward to refilling our supply.
text_fidelity_b: IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens

Winning Moves Games Brainspin Creativity Game (1198) Such a simple yet creative little game. It literally takes seconds to explain the game and just a few rounds to master the idea. I love that it opens the mind to creative imagination.

The goal is to look at a simple glyph, then right doen as many unique things it reminds you of. For example, a simple square could be a sandbox, a sandwich or a corral. Each person writes as many of these as they can in a minute then take turns reading their list. If your idea is unique and no one else came up with it, you get a point. If someone else has it, you both cross it out. Ideas are juried by yhe players so you can't just say ridiculous stuff to be unique.

We played a number of rounds and they were boisterous and sometimes heated when people refused to count questionable ideas. But for the most part it was a great, quick game with more than a few laughs.

Only thing I wish was that it came with its own timer. We ended up grabbing one from another game.

Melissa & Doug Children's Book - Poke-a-Dot: An Alphabet Eye Spy (Board Book with Buttons to Pop) - Alphabet Pop It Book, Push Pop Book For Toddlers And Kids Ages 3+ The Pop-a-Dots are a novel tactile experience for any little kid. The initial excitement is lots of fun. The color pallet is bright. The layout of the book is excellent:
1. The beginning of the book contains 14 pages showing 2 letters of the alphabet, per page, with a “Look for:” list of words at the bottom of the page. There are Pop-a-Dots for 1, 2 or 3 objects, per page.

2. Next, there are 5 pages of upper case letters of the alphabet. Each letter has the head of an animal beginning with that letter and a Pop-a-Dot. There is a “Can you find” word list of the animals at the bottom of each page.

3. The final page is an alphabet grid. Each block of the grid shows both the upper and lower case letter as well as an object. The full upper case alphabet and lower case alphabet run across the top and bottom of the page, respectively.

I give 5 stars for the font, punctuation and correct relative sizing of upper and lower case used throughout the book. Excellent!

There are some challenges for the intended age group, in my opinion, that I would like to share.

Potential Challenges (imho):
1. When this arrived, the first thing that struck me is the weight of this book. It is too heavy for me to hold while reading alone or with a toddler. Book is recommended for ages 3-6 yrs. and those little ones could not hold this book. The only comfortable way to read it is opened flat on a table or the floor.

2. The structure of the binding prevents the pages from laying flat when the book is open on a table. The binding will be damaged/tear if a child presses down on the book trying to make the pages lay flat, specifically the pages in the middle of the book. You can see in my pics the stress creases already showing at the inner binding edge of the first and last pages just from me flipping thru the pages for 15 minutes, or so.

3. I am on the fence about the artwork (perhaps just a personal aesthetic) and choice of some items used to represent the letters. For example, I had no idea what a Xolo was. I had to google it to find out it is a rare breed of hairless dog. I dont find the artwork for Quail, Iguana, Vulture, Ice or Gorilla to be easily recognizable to a child. Yoyo, Nail, Wig are not common objects for this age group. ( I checked the copyright date to ensure this was not an older book where a yoyo would be a known object. Copyright is 2019)

All in all, the Pop-a-Dots are THE selling feature of this book. Kids love to pop them and the sound they make. If you are looking for a novel gift, this would be a great choice. As far as a learning tool, this would not be among my top choices.

I hope the pics below will clarify my thoughts on this book. Thanks!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Children's Book - Poke-a-Dot: An Alphabet Eye Spy (Board Book with Buttons to Pop) - Alphabet Pop It Book, Push Pop Book For Toddlers And Kids Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up I think I'm just a bit too spoiled by the Pandemic Legacy games, Kings Dilemma, Crusoe Crew, Above and Below, and the like.

The Adventures of Robin Hood is a fine game that is meant to be a legacy-like experience - you play a pretty straightforward move-around-the-board style game, trying to stay inside the shadows printed on the board, until you need to pop out to land on one of a few dozen removable/flippable cardboard cutout pieces that populate the boards. Once you land there to complete objectives, you read a few lines from a book based on the mission at hand, and sometimes you need to perform well at a little combat or make a decision on what to say.

The game is easy to learn and offers a very different gaming experience for those who are unfamiliar with the aforementioned legacy games. Unfortunately, if you've played those, this one is likely just a bit too juvenile. Reading from the book is fun at first, until you find yourself going through the motions and making very similar decisions about completely uninteresting plot points as you progress. Characters largely say the same things, all lead you more or less directly to where you need to go, and when you get there and succeed, you get a "congratulations" rather than a different gaming experience (like in Pandemic), new challenges (like Kings Dilemma) or even a remarkable story experience (like Above and Below). Everything just kind of plays out on it's own.

If you have an impatient bunch, the "pick the next player" from the bag thing could leave people waiting quite a while between turns.

The other thing I don't like is that the rules are a bit interpretive in terms of how movement and the shadows rules affect players. If you want to play this "by the rules" and you have someone who wants to argue over a millimeter, the rules will allow the fudger to make pretty much any interpretation they wish. Most missions are also very much on the easy side.

As this is aimed at a younger audience (I think - the box says 10+ age), some of this is quite forgivable, but for the mature gamer, you have far better options, even if you're enamored with the theme, as I am, or the legacy style game, as my family is. The little one was bored by the long missions, Mom and Dad were thinking there should just be a little more punch to the story. Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift Wow, is this a toy? Because it is full of problems and inaccuracies. I’d like to start with my side-by-side photo showing some of the most egregious problems.
On the right hand with a black background is how it is supposed to look, and on the left is how it actually looks.
*Spinal alignment: any human with this type of alignment has a serious medical condition. The spine is supposed to have curvature in order to support the weight properly. As you can see by the Sideview of this toy, there is minimal curvature, and what little there is would lead the person to fall backwards. This is particularly problematic along the cervical and lumbar vertebrae (neck and lower back)
*The ribcage on this silly toy flares out at the bottom in a bizzarre way that doesn’t represent normal anatomy. Likewise, there is no attempt to indicate where the bone ends and the cartilaginous attachment points begin. Our ribs are not solid bone all the way from the vertebral column to the sternum. There’s supposed to be cartilage toward the midline as the ribs approach the sternum. Even if this model can’t indicate that, there should at least have been some sort of scoring or line or something.
The radius and ulna are ridiculous. Their thickness and size are not in correct proportion with the rest of the body. Also, why is this not in anatomical position?
Then there’s the attachment from the humerus to the glenoid fossa of the scapula, which cannot be seen in the poster or in this model. That’s just not how our arms are attached at all. Like the hip joint, the shoulder is a ball and socket joint, albeit a much shallower one than the hips. The way this is attached is so misleading and terrible. I can’t even deal with it. And circling back once again to the alignment of the spine, the pelvic bowl is completely wrong. It’s supposed to tilt downward much more.
So basically this is garbage. It’s not good for art, and it’s not really good for teaching either. What a shame. It did have some things going for it, but the issues I pointed out are too significant to ignore.
The included poster is OK, and so are a few of the skull details. It gets to stars for effort and that. But it’s pretty obvious to me that whoever designed this doesn’t know their anatomy. Imagine how much better they could’ve done if they actually paid a professional to do the design before manufacturing hundreds (thousands?) of useless little skeletons.
text_fidelity_b: Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels T-Rex Rampage Track Set, Works City Sets, Toys for Boys Ages 5 to 10 My son has several sets of Hot Wheels toys. Hot Wheels is often hit or miss. They sometimes have a great idea and an awesomely executed toy. Sometimes the toys create nothing but frustration. However, with this playset my really had nothing but fear. Therefore, the Mattel Hot Wheels City T-Rex Rampage has done it's job. It strikes fear in all those who come upon it. My 7 year old is afraid of this toy. He was ok with it until he found out that the T-Rex moved, and it's no dice. He doesn't even want it just sitting in his room.

After you figure out how to put it together. The T-Rex part was tricky, but don't worry the part can come apart so if you mess up the alignment, you're ok. You get 1 angry T-Rex who needs a snack and a nap, 2 buildings, a launchpad, and a piece of track and a car. I'm not sure what the name of the game is. I am not entirely sure what you are supposed to do. My son comes up with different ideas every 5 minutes. However, the scary part comes in when you turn it on. The toy comes with batteries and when you turn it on and push the blue button on the circle track, the T-Rex will start to thrash around and knock over buildings etc. He roars and all of this action is what scares my son. The launcher is of course his favorite part. If you launch the car just right, the car will hit a button to "defeat" the dinosaur.

The ultimate issue with Hot Wheels is that except for the cars themselves, most sets get broken fairly quickly. I cannot say the same for this because it's not getting much play. As with all Hot Wheel sets you can connect them to each other if you have enough track to do so. So, that is the best part about Hot Wheels. However, tracks are hard to come by and they are usually long and flimsy. So, you can't really link up the sets and the tracks get all bent out of shape. I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

These are not bad cards at all. They’re beautiful and they’re well made, and they have some incredible artwork. However, the color scheme is not the best and these cards would be even better if the background and black suit colors were chosen a little more thoughtfully.

Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit I thought this would be a cool activity to do with my 6 year old. She LOVES crafts, and I actually bought a coloring "stained glass" art book by Klutz for her in the past (which she loved)
It was a little hard to tell exactly what the process was of making them just by looking at the pictures, and It was actually a bit more difficult than I assumed.

So you take the colored film paper, trace the shape out of the book, cut it out, then place it on the sticky paper to puzzle all the colored pieces together like a mosaic, to make up the whole picture. You youths choose to do them any color you want, but the more colors you use to make up the picture, the more patience and precision you will need.
We started off simple with the strawberry (only 2 colors) which was pretty easy.
I went to apply the puff paint and it would not come out of the top of the tube. I tried to cut the nozzle down, squeeze it out slow which ended in it coming out the side of the bottle, and getting all over my fingers. It was so thick, I assumed it got semi dried out, so I threw it away to prevent any further mess.
Since we were unable to use the puff paint, my daughter outlined the strawberry with black sharpie. Unfortunately without the puff paint, the film paper is pretty flimsy.
Even though we did not get the full effect of the project, we still had some fun doing the craft together.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit

Zobmondo!! GoLo! Golf Dice Game for Families and Kids, Award-Winning Fun Game for Home or Travel, Quick to Learn, For 1+ Players, Ages 6 and Up This game is pretty simple. Each time you take the dice you'll basically be playing nine holes of golf. The dice are set up with 2 for par 3 holes, 2 for par 5, and the remaining 5 for par four holes. When you start you'll roll all 9 dice. You must keep at least one, but can reroll all the others, and you continue to reroll until you've set aside all 9 dice at which point you score the dice.

Its that simple. Lowest score over X number of holes wins (the game suggests playing 8 rounds to simulate a full 4 day golf tournament).

Fun, portable and very easy to play. It does have the downside of basically being completely random, and in someways its a variation on Yahtzee, but its well themed. If you want a good dice game for trips and don't want Yahtzee, this is a good one to choose.
text_fidelity_b: Zobmondo!! GoLo! Golf Dice Game for Families and Kids, Award-Winning Fun Game for Home or Travel, Quick to Learn, For 1+ Players, Ages 6 and Up

Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack The Barbie Dream Closet is indeed a very happy dream realized. There’s so much space to store all of the clothes and accessories, as well any additional clothing items you already own for Barbie. The mini hangers work great with the clothing rack, as there’s a bit of a grip to the hooks so the hangers stay in place, but are easy to put on and take off. The system is also super convenient to carry around due to its folded design, which latches in the front with a Barbie labeled lever, and the handle on top lets this go anywhere with ease. I do love that this set encourages all sorts of ways to be fun, adventurous, sporty, fancy, and smart with the closet decals, clothes and accessories (lab coat and shoes, laptop, fancy dress with jewelry and shoes, scuba gear, etc).

A few criticisms though…the nob on top to turn the clothing rack is a bit hard to spin, both in resistance and due to the short nob. I do wish it was a little bit looser and the nob was a little bit taller to make it easier to grab.
There are a few areas that fold in and out for storage, as well as shelves to place things, but I think it would have been nice for some sort of drawer system. The drawers would have been helpful for storing the mini bracelet, necklace, hair brush, sunglasses, etc to give them a good home when not in use. Using my imagination, it would have been extra fun if the full-length mirror had a battery operated set of mini Hollywood lights to add some flare. I think some extra touches like the drawers and mirror lights would make the price worth it. I think it’s just a tad on the expensive side for it lacking some details, although it's worth reiterating that the included pieces offer a lot of good play and imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack

I had to try this one out.

If you've never used an infinity cube before, they're the latest in fun fidgety-toy types of thing, but also kind of more interesting because they bend and fold in ways that feel like it is constantly turning into something else. Sort like a transformer toy that goes on forever.

I really like the wood color and style of this, but my first impression wasn't very good. It was a lot harder to move and the wooden blocks would get stuck on each other as you bend and fold. Not anywhere near as smooth as the plastic variants. But the cords that hold this together just need some stretching to loosen them up. Once you've broken it in, it moves much more smoothly and eventually will give you the satisfying feel that an infinity cube is known for. I can't speak for the longevity of it yet, I am a little concerned that in the same way you need to break this in, it can also eventually stretch out and/or snap. But so far it's holding up and by then, I'm guessing a new fidget toy will be the latest craze.
